title: Your Attitude: Stance Adverbs and Kinetic Art

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *francamente* and stance adverbs from B2 Unit 1: *francamente*, *lamentablemente*, *en realidad*, *en rigor*. They step outside the sentence and say how the speaker feels about the fact, and a comma marks each edge. Talking about art invites opinions, so they are useful here.

sections.title: Adverbs that show your attitude
rows: En realidad, Soto nació en Ciudad Bolívar, no en Caracas.
*en realidad*: you correct what someone assumed
En rigor, Cruz-Diez nació en Caracas.
*en rigor*: you give the exact truth
Lamentablemente, no puedo ver la exposición esta semana.
Francamente, la obra de Cruz-Diez me parece fascinante.
*francamente*: you are direct about your opinion

items.spanish: En realidad, Soto nació en Ciudad Bolívar.
items.english: Actually, Soto was born in Ciudad Bolívar.

items.spanish: Lamentablemente, no puedo ver la exposición esta semana.
items.english: Unfortunately, I cannot see the exhibition this week.

items.spanish: Francamente, la obra de Cruz-Diez me parece fascinante.
items.english: Frankly, Cruz-Diez's work seems fascinating to me.

items.spanish: En Ciudad Bolívar, precisamente su ciudad natal, está el Museo Soto.
items.english: In Ciudad Bolívar, precisely his home town, is the Soto Museum.

sections.content: Try the comma test: if you can pause and put commas around the adverb, it comments on the whole sentence. *Precisamente* takes no commas, because it points at the word after it. Use one stance adverb per sentence; two in a row sound heavy.
